architecture_notes: All kp.scripts lifecycle functions are callable from any installed Lua state, including the console state, but the one process-wide Host queues load/unload/reload work. Host::service_requests runs the queued operation at a host lifecycle service boundary; this is process-local API behavior rather than proof of a client or server process.

kp.events.register/unregister mutate a per-script Lua callback registry. A later callback inherits the logical side of the dispatch site recorded for that event; registration alone supplies no live dispatch proof.

kp.harness functions are installed in each Lua state and invoke the traced native path recorded per row. The surface deliberately mixes client GUI, server mutations, client-to-server requests, both-side reads/operations, process-local metadata/event transport, and stored-result accessors. The engine_side field follows the concrete adapter implementation; it is not inferred from the Lua callback thread or process role.
The source manifest reports 111 event constants. Constant names, including dead names, are not callable registrations and must not be assigned server/client side merely from spelling.
